Replay

Slopball3D session UI

4 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Native checkpoint savesPlay againBrowser-local checkpoints

play.sh opens Solo, Host, Join and Watch controls with name/address/port. The default port remains 49580. Host waits for the first connected player to Start; Solo starts automatically. RS3_PLAYERS and RS3_GOALS set the minimum roster and winning score. Explicit RS3_ROLE launches retain the automatic fixture path.

WASD moves on XZ and Space kicks with loft. Enter opens chat; Escape releases focus while preserving the draft. Typing suppresses movement and kick edges while the owned ball continues its normal solver/observation path. Chat is literal, including markup characters. Named observers retain seat zero. Tab shows authoritative names, teams, score and measured ping; departed rows remain until reused.

Leave freezes the bodies, resets their local driver/sample state and disables collisions while disconnected. Rejoin reseeds current authority state and restores each scene's authored collision layers/masks. Skin position and quaternion are restored before reattachment. Identity, seat and match score survive rejoin.

Native identity/name preferences use user://replay_slopball3d_identity and its adjacent .name file. RS3_PROFILE selects another prefix. Explicit tokens, bots and RS3_PERSIST=0 bypass storage. Malformed names are refused and preserved. Name submission bookkeeping resets after an authority epoch change.

The UI/HUD layers scale to the visible viewport; camera and physics scenes remain unchanged. Names and manual start are replayable values/commands. Waiting rejects solver observations at the reducer as well as disabling local controls. Content D4 (0x52534c4f50334434) identifies the changed world/action schema. D1/D2/D3 peers/checkpoints require an explicit conversion; none is supplied here.

The established Body3 ownership handshake, interpolation and solver seeding remain. This does not replay contact caches/joints or add netgraph parity. Original Slopball3D and the separate 2D port remain intact.

Native checkpoint saves#

The menu selects a save file; the default is user://slopball3d.replay, configurable with RS3_SAVE. Save/F5 is available to a standalone native authority. A failed staging write preserves the prior completed file. A successful later save replaces it. Clients and configured Rooms cannot use this direct file-save path.

Resume solo/host requires the profile of the saved host. It installs the exact checkpoint in a new epoch, then the owner-stream driver rebinds and seeds the local solver from authority state before publishing fresh observations. Other saved peers are scheduled to leave; the same profiles can rejoin their reserved seats. Match settings, names, score, ownership scopes, pose/momentum and movement baselines are restored. Shared file-resume policy retires pending commands; it is separate from coordinated migration.

Missing, malformed/incompatible, wrong-owner, protected-policy and exhausted-epoch saves are refused without replacing existing data. Native chat history is not part of the game checkpoint, and solver contacts/joints are not serialized. Public deployment requires separate integration. This save UI uses the existing model schema.

Play again#

After a match finishes, its first connected player can choose Play again when the minimum roster is present. This is a round-scoped command inside the same session. It rejects guests, observers, stale round numbers and exhausted revision counters. Names, seats, connected/departed flags and match settings survive.

The reset clears scores, per-match counters, player/ball poses and momentum, challenges and pending offers, and starts a new kickoff hold. Every body receives a newer ownership revision; old samples and old offer scopes cannot publish into the new match. The reset is built as a candidate so exhaustion cannot partially change the world. The standard Body adapter reseeds from those new scopes.

Gameplay events also identify their round, and new-round presentation ignores old goal effects. The UI resets local kick/button/report state without reconnecting. The original game interface has no Play again control; this is a Replay addition.

See Party and browser play for service-backed invitations, stored credentials, handoff and publication through Save/F5.

Browser-local checkpoints#

Browser Solo uses named slots instead of native file paths. The default slot is pitch; the save_slot URL parameter selects another. Names accept 1–48 ASCII letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores. Slots belong to the current browser origin/profile and personal identity; they do not synchronize between devices.

Save/F5 captures the current checkpoint once and reports completion after its IndexedDB write. Leave is blocked during that write. Resume solo waits for both identity and slot loading, restores the exact saved world in a newer epoch, and seeds the local physics bodies before new observations can commit. A URL with role=solo&resume=1&save_slot=pitch uses the same asynchronous loading sequence.

Two tabs cannot silently overwrite each other's progress: a stale revision fails and keeps the committed slot. Unreadable slots and malformed identity data are preserved. Choose another valid slot or reload after a conflict; Resume is disabled when no readable checkpoint is available. Play again can be saved in the same slot.

Native file saves keep their existing host-profile policy. Party Save/F5 publishes through the service and does not create or replace a browser-local checkpoint. Local slots store game state, not a promise to preserve cosmetic chat or Godot solver contact caches. Clearing the browser's site data removes its local records.

See browser-save results and limitations.
